system:
You are a computational cancer biologist searching CRISPR screen data for selective genetic dependencies: genes that cancer cells with a particular alteration (the biomarker) need more than other cancer cells do. Such genes are candidate drug targets with a built-in patient-selection strategy.

Work like a careful scientist:
1. Plan first with write_plan, and revise it as you learn.
2. Survey the data (genome_wide_top, scan_biomarker, scan_target) to generate candidate hypotheses.
3. Be sceptical before you believe a signal. Use inspect_association to check whether it is driven by one lineage or a disease subtype hiding inside a lineage, and whether the effect is large enough to matter. Ask whether the biology makes sense (paralog buffering, pathway dependence, oncogene addiction). A broadly essential target may lack a therapeutic window.
4. Check the literature with search_pubmed before registering, and judge novelty honestly.
5. Register only your best hypotheses (register_hypothesis). Registration is final and must come before replication. You have 5 replications, each of which must pass one-sided p < 0.01 in BOTH held-out Broad cell lines and independent Sanger screens.
6. Report honestly with submit_findings. A hypothesis is replicated only if replicate() said so. Negative results are results. Never let what you remember from the literature override what the data show.

You have at most 30 model turns. Batch independent tool calls in one turn.
task_prompt:
Mission: Search freely for the most promising selective dependencies in the data.

Goal: identify up to 5 candidate selective dependencies, and favour candidates that are NOT already well established in the literature, since rediscovering textbook biology is not the aim. Pre-register, replicate, and submit honest findings, including failures.

I'm scanning through a few candidate gene pairs. The SYNJ2 to HERPUD1 link looks mostly driven by lymphoid B-cell samples and stays negative even after adjusting for lineage, so it could reflect a lymphoid or plasma cell program. HERPUD1 is an ER stress gene, which makes it less novel, though it's still worth a look. Next I'm turning to the ADCY6 loss pair.

I'm checking the ADCY6 loss against RUNX1, which is lymphoid-enriched at 36 samples with a strong negative within myeloid. Next I'm weighing EHD4 to RAC2, which looks like a hematopoietic dependency and seems less interesting, and POLD1 to PRPS2, which is colorectal and MSI-like with a possible PRPS1 buffering angle at only n=6. I'm also glancing at PER1 to MYH14, which probably amounts to noise. Then I'll widen the scan to mutation-type pairs with larger counts.

content.thinking: All three attempts came back negative, so I'm reporting that as it is. The discovery signals seem to have come from lineage effects and small samples, and none of them held up on replication. The H3 effect was mostly driven by lymphoid cells and weakened out of sample. I'm submitting it.

findings.claim: Damaging TRRAP mutation was associated with KIDINS220 dependency in discovery lines (n=8, 4/8 strongly dependent vs ~9% of others, lineage-independent), but this did not hold in held-out Broad lines (p=0.17) or Sanger (p=0.16).

Damaging POLD1 mutation was associated with PRPS2 dependency in discovery lines (n=6, mostly colorectal), with no signal in held-out Broad (p=0.58) or Sanger (p=0.98); the discovery signal was very small-n and likely chance or lineage-driven.

SYNJ2 expression loss was associated with HERPUD1 dependency, driven mainly by B-lymphoid lines (22 altered, 9 strongly dependent vs 3/562 others); it attenuated and failed in held-out Broad (p=0.086) and Sanger (p=0.94), so it is not a robust pan-lineage selective dependency.

input.summary: I surveyed 626 discovery lines for lineage-adjusted biomarker->dependency pairs. The strongest genome-wide hits (e.g., LOSS_ANXA4/LOSS_JUN/LOSS_ZNF629 -> PAX5/IRF4/HERPUD1, LOSS_GNA11 -> MEF2C) were dominated by lymphoid, melanoma or other single-lineage contexts, and many rested on very small numbers of altered lines. I pre-registered three candidates with some novelty (MUT_TRRAP->KIDINS220, MUT_POLD1->PRPS2, LOSS_SYNJ2->HERPUD1). PubMed searches found no prior synthetic-lethal reports for these pairs. None replicated: effects shrank toward zero in held-out Broad lines and Sanger screens, and in each case the discovery signal was carried by a handful of lines. Lesson: these discovery signals are fragile, and the only robust-looking patterns were lineage-confounded. No candidate is recommended for follow-up. I did not test any candidate with the remaining 2 replication credits.

findings.claim: Damaging TRRAP mutation was associated with KIDINS220 dependency in discovery lines (n=8, 4/8 strongly dependent vs ~9% of others, lineage-independent), but this did not hold in held-out Broad lines (p=0.17) or Sanger (p=0.16).

Damaging POLD1 mutation was associated with PRPS2 dependency in discovery lines (n=6, mostly colorectal), with no signal in held-out Broad (p=0.58) or Sanger (p=0.98); the discovery signal was very small-n and likely chance or lineage-driven.

SYNJ2 expression loss was associated with HERPUD1 dependency, driven mainly by B-lymphoid lines (22 altered, 9 strongly dependent vs 3/562 others); it attenuated and failed in held-out Broad (p=0.086) and Sanger (p=0.94), so it is not a robust pan-lineage selective dependency.

input.summary: I surveyed 626 discovery lines for lineage-adjusted biomarker->dependency pairs. The strongest genome-wide hits (e.g., LOSS_ANXA4/LOSS_JUN/LOSS_ZNF629 -> PAX5/IRF4/HERPUD1, LOSS_GNA11 -> MEF2C) were dominated by lymphoid, melanoma or other single-lineage contexts, and many rested on very small numbers of altered lines. I pre-registered three candidates with some novelty (MUT_TRRAP->KIDINS220, MUT_POLD1->PRPS2, LOSS_SYNJ2->HERPUD1). PubMed searches found no prior synthetic-lethal reports for these pairs. None replicated: effects shrank toward zero in held-out Broad lines and Sanger screens, and in each case the discovery signal was carried by a handful of lines. Lesson: these discovery signals are fragile, and the only robust-looking patterns were lineage-confounded. No candidate is recommended for follow-up. I did not test any candidate with the remaining 2 replication credits.

output: Findings recorded.
